Personality: Larch is a quintessential hot-blooded young Battanian who, at just eighteen years old, is already known for his reckless audacity. His character brims with primal martial vigor, and on the battlefield he always charges at the vanguard, eager to prove himself through sheer strength and skill. Unbound by mercy or a sense of honor, his conduct is cold and direct, never tangling itself in moral dilemmas or complex calculations of interest. To him, generosity is the disguise of the weak, and only the polearm and heavy sword in his hands can be truly relied upon. He has no ambition to become a far-sighted statesman, preferring to remain a pure warrior. Such fearless recklessness wins him admiration among young nobles of his generation, though it also makes him overly harsh and impatient when handling diplomacy and fief administration—a pragmatist who believes only in strength.
Background: Larch hails from Battania's foremost house, Clan fen Gruffendoc, as the son of Minsel. Growing up in Marunath under the rule of High King Caladog, he witnessed firsthand how his family rose from obscurity to become the core of the kingdom. In Battania—a realm that reveres personal martial prowess and where clan chieftains each harbor their own designs—he knows well that stable power rests upon absolute force. As a devoted follower of Caladog, he staunchly upholds the High King's authority, seeking to guide the unruly clan leaders with a firm hand. Young though he is, he has already mastered a variety of weapons, excelling particularly with polearms and two-handed swords. He is not only an heir to his clan's glory, but a sharp blade in Caladog's drive for centralized rule, ever ready to fight in defense of his family's interests at Uthelaim Castle, Rhemtoil Castle, and beyond.
